pr.title: Simplify `align_of_val::<[T]>(…)` → `align_of::<T>()`
pr.description: I spotted this while working on the inliner (rust-lang/rust#144561).  In particular, if [`Layout::for_value`](https://doc.rust-lang.org/std/alloc/struct.Layout.html#method.for_value) inlines, then it can be pretty easy to end up with an `align_of_val::<[T]>` today (demo: <https://rust.godbolt.org/z/Tesnscj4a>) where we can save at least a block, if not more, by using the version that's an rvalue and not a call.
pr.author: scottmcm

processing.reason: The PR adds a semantically sound optimization, so there is no historical wrong transformation to validate. Source inspection (tests/mir-opt/instsimplify/align_of_slice.of_val_slice.InstSimplify-after-simplifycfg.diff and instsimplify.rs) shows the only change is replacing a call `align_of_val::<[T]>(ptr)` with the rvalue `AlignOf(T)` plus a `goto` to the original destination block. Both forms are defined to return the ABI alignment of the slice, and for a slice `[T]` the alignment is by definition `align_of::<T>()` independent of the length metadata; the element type of a slice is always `Sized`. The guard restricts the rewrite to `ty::Slice(elem_ty)`, so trait objects and other unsized types are not affected. The call's single argument is a pointer/reference operand with no side effects, the intrinsic is non-unwinding, and the destination and successor block are preserved. Thus the pre-PR call form and the post-PR folded form produce identical values for every defined input; the frozen analysis's “incorrect transformation” is simply the older unoptimized baseline, not a semantic error. Any pair engineered to differ would have to invent an unrelated return-value change (e.g., using metadata or a different element type), which the task forbids. Therefore no source-grounded counterexample exists.

analysis.summary: InstSimplify gains a scalar-replacement rewrite for calls to the `align_of_val` intrinsic when the value's type is a slice: `align_of_val::<[T]>(ptr)` becomes the nullary `AlignOf(T)` rvalue plus a `goto`, eliminating the call and its metadata-dependent argument while preserving the destination and successor block. The pass is deliberately run after inlining so that inlined `Layout::for_value`/`align_of_val_raw` code can be collapsed.
analysis.originalLogic: Before the change, MIR for a slice value alignment query remained a call terminator, e.g. `_0 = std::intrinsics::align_of_val::<[T]>(move _2) -> [return: bb1, unwind unreachable];`. The MIR pass `InstSimplify` invoked only `simplify_primitive_clone`, `simplify_intrinsic_assert`, `simplify_nounwind_call`, `simplify_duplicate_switch_targets` (and friends), with no handling of slice `align_of_val`. The PR rationale states: "Convert `align_of_val::<[T]>(ptr)` to `align_of::<T>()`, since the alignment of a slice doesn't actually depend on metadata at all and the element type is always `Sized`."
analysis.incorrectTransformation: The transformation to test is the historical absence/incorrectness of the slice simplification: a call to `align_of_val::<[T]>(ptr)` is left as an intrinsic call instead of being folded. Do not invent the reverse rewrite (turning `AlignOf(T)` into an `align_of_val` call); the erroneous baseline is the unoptimized call form. The corrected output replaces the call with `_0 = AlignOf(T); goto -> bb1;` (the destination block). The relevant guard conditions in the patch are: terminator is `TerminatorKind::Call { func, args, destination, target: Some(destination_block), .. }`, `args.len() == 1`, `func.const_fn_def()` yields `(fn_def_id, generics)`, `self.tcx.is_intrinsic(fn_def_id, sym::align_of_val)`, and `ty::Slice(elem_ty) = *generics.type_at(0).kind()`.
analysis.inputDomain: MIR functions containing a one-argument call to the `align_of_val` intrinsic whose single type generic is a slice `[T]`, typically arising directly from `core::intrinsics::align_of_val(slice)` or after inlining `Layout::for_value`/`align_of_val_raw` on `[T]`. The element `T` is implicitly `Sized`. Non-slice unsized types and zero/multiple-argument calls are outside the matched domain.
analysis.trigger: A MIR `Call` terminator to `std::intrinsics::align_of_val::<[T]>` with exactly one argument, a resolvable `const_fn_def`, `is_intrinsic(fn_def_id, sym::align_of_val)`, and `generics.type_at(0)` whose kind is `ty::Slice(elem_ty)`, and a `Some(destination_block)` call target.
preconditions: The pass runs as `InstSimplify`, including after inlining, as noted: "This is here so it can run after inlining, where it's more useful. (LowerIntrinsics is done in cleanup, before the optimization passes.)"
The intrinsic's type argument (generics.type_at(0)) must be a slice, not the pointer argument type: `let ty::Slice(elem_ty) = *generics.type_at(0).kind()`.
The call must have `target: Some(destination_block)` so the rewrite can emit `TerminatorKind::Goto { target: *destination_block }`.
The call must have exactly one argument: `args.len() == 1`.
The call must be resolved to the `align_of_val` intrinsic via `func.const_fn_def()` and `is_intrinsic(fn_def_id, sym::align_of_val)`.
pitfalls: Do not use the argument pointer's pointee type instead of the intrinsic type argument; the patch matches `generics.type_at(0).kind()` for `ty::Slice(elem_ty)`.
Only slice types are handled; do not generalise the `AlignOf(T)` rewrite to arbitrary unsized types such as trait objects where metadata can affect alignment.

The rewrite must preserve the original call destination and jump to the original destination block: it pushes `StatementKind::Assign(destination, Rvalue::NullaryOp(NullOp::AlignOf, elem_ty))` and sets the terminator to a `Goto` to `destination_block`.
The inserted statement must carry the terminator's `source_info`.
This belongs in `InstSimplify` (post-inlining), not in `LowerIntrinsics`, because the opportunity appears after inlining `Layout::for_value`.
Do not treat the test diff's old call line as evidence that the new pass is wrong; the retained test name/comment does not establish correctness, compare actual value assignments.
analysis.testStrategy: Add a mir-opt test using `//@ test-mir-pass: InstSimplify-after-simplifycfg`, `//@ needs-unwind`, `#![crate_type = \"lib\"]`, `#![feature(core_intrinsics)]`, and an `EMIT_MIR align_of_slice.of_val_slice.InstSimplify-after-simplifycfg.diff` directive. The function should be `pub fn of_val_slice<T>(slice: &[T]) -> usize { unsafe { core::intrinsics::align_of_val(slice) } }` with `// CHECK-LABEL: fn of_val_slice(_1: &[T])` and `// CHECK: _0 = AlignOf(T);`, asserting the call is replaced by the rvalue and goto. Additionally add a `tests/mir-opt/pre-codegen/drop_boxed_slice.rs` test with `//@ compile-flags: -O -Zmir-opt-level=2`, `EMIT_MIR_FOR_EACH_PANIC_STRATEGY`, `EMIT_MIR_FOR_EACH_BIT_WIDTH`, checking an inlined `<Box<[T]> as Drop>::drop` where `size_of_val::<[T]>` remains a call but `AlignOf(T)` appears and feeds `__rust_dealloc` through the `Alignment` transmute/discriminant path. Check the generated pre-codegen MIR for 32/64-bit and panic-abort/panic-unwind variants.
